Its products include foods, beverages, cleaning agents, personal care products and other consumer staples. The company was established in India in 1931 as Hindustan Vanaspati Manufacturing Co. Following a merger of constituent groups in 1956, it was renamed Hindustan Lever Limited. The company was renamed again in June 2007 as Hindustan Unilever Limited.{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/transition-to-new-name-was-smooth-hul/207944/|title=Transition to new name was smooth: HUL|last=Srinivasan|first=Lalitha|date=31 July 2007|publisher=The Financial Express|location=Mumbai|access-date=31 October 2013|archive-date=3 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103212335/http://www.financialexpress.com/news/transition-to-new-name-was-smooth-hul/207944|url-status=live}} Hindustan Unilever has been at the helm of a lot of controversies, such as dumping highly toxic [[Mercury (element)|mercury]]-contaminated waste in regular dumps, contaminating the land and water of [[Kodaikanal]]. (See: [[Kodaikanal mercury poisoning]]). The British-Dutch company also faced major flak for an advertising campaign covering the Hindu pilgrimage site at [[Kumbh Mela]] in a negative light, calling it a "place where old people get abandoned,"{{Cite web |date=7 March 2019 |title=Hindustan Unilever faces flak over Red Label ad showing son 'abandoning' father at Kumbh Mela |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/retail/hindustan-unilever-faces-flak-over-red-label-ad-showing-son-abandoning-father-at-kumbh-mela-2518541.htm |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=#BoycottHindustanUnilever Trends After Ad On Kumbh Mela Faces Criticism |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kumb-mela-ad-boycotthindustanunilever-trends-after-red-label-tea-ad-faces-criticism-2004261 |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=NDTV.com |archive-date=25 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725002415/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kumb-mela-ad-boycotthindustanunilever-trends-after-red-label-tea-ad-faces-criticism-2004261 |url-status=live }} a move that was termed racist and insensitive. In December 2018 HUL announced its acquisition of [[GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals|GlaxoSmithKline]] India's consumer business for US$3.8 billion in an all-equity merger deal with a 1:4.39 ratio.{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/top-story/hindustan-unilever-limitedhulglaxosmithklinegsk-chhorlicksboost/story/296927.html|title=GSK Consumer Healthcare to merge with Hindustan Unilever: Here are 10 things you should know|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=3 December 2018|access-date=8 March 2019|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327085751/https://www.businesstoday.in/top-story/hindustan-unilever-limitedhulglaxosmithklinegsk-chhorlicksboost/story/296927.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/hul-gsk-deal-3800-employees-face-uncertainty-decision-awaited/story/297981.html|title=HUL-GSK deal: 3,800 employees face uncertainty, decision awaited|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=6 December 2018|access-date=8 March 2019|archive-date=4 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904121341/https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy-politics/story/hul-gsk-deal-3800-employees-face-uncertainty-decision-awaited-118923-2018-12-06|url-status=live}} However, the integration of GSK's 3,800 employees remained uncertain as HUL stated there was no clause for retention of employees in the deal. In April 2020, HUL completed its merger with GlaxoSmithKline Consumer Healthcare (GSKCH India) after completing all legal procedures.{{cite news|url=https://business.medicaldialogues.in/hul-expects-to-complete-merger-with-gsk-consumer-healthcare-in-2019/ |title=HUL expects to complete merger with GSK Consumer Healthcare in 2019|access-date=20 January 2019 | work=Medical Dialogues |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829010101/https://business.medicaldialogues.in/hul%2Dexpects%2Dto%2Dcomplete%2Dmerger%2Dwith%2Dgsk%2Dconsumer%2Dhealthcare%2Din%2D2019/|url-status=dead |archive-date=29 August 2012 }} ==Presence== Hindustan Unilever's corporate headquarters are located in [[Andheri]], [[Mumbai]]. The campus is spread over 12.5 acres of land and houses over 1,600 employees.{{cite web |url=http://www.hul.co.in/mediacentre/news/2010/HULMovesToNewCampus.aspx |title=HUL moves to new campus | 2010 | Hindustan Unilever |publisher=Hindustan Unilever |access-date=12 July 2012 |archive-date=22 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120622233943/http://www.hul.co.in/mediacentre/news/2010/HULMovesToNewCampus.aspx |url-status=live }} The Campus is designed by Mumbai-based architecture firm Kapadia Associates.{{Cite web|url=http://www.livemint.com/Leisure/SM1DA6bKK9PUvonWPMmlQJ/Designed-for-leverage.html|title=Designed for leverage – Livemint|website=livemint.com|date=3 February 2010|access-date=16 December 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220175320/http://www.livemint.com/Leisure/SM1DA6bKK9PUvonWPMmlQJ/Designed-for-leverage.html|url-status=live}} The company's previous headquarters were located in Backbay Reclamation, Mumbai at the Lever House, where it was housed for more than 46 years.{{cite web|url=http://www.aifl.net/CompanyProfile/Company_Profile.aspx?id=93&FinCode=100696|title=Atlas Integrated Finance Ltd|publisher=Aifl.net|access-date=10 February 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103183229/http://www.aifl.net/CompanyProfile/Company_Profile.aspx?id=93&FinCode=100696|archive-date=3 November 2013}} The Hindustan Unilever Research Centre (HURC) was set up in 1966 in [[Mumbai]], and Unilever Research India in [[Bangalore]] in 1997. In 2006, the company's research facilities were brought together at a single site in Bangalore.[http://www.hul.co.in/careers-redesign/carreerschoices/researchanddevelopment/OverviewofResearchCentres/ Overview of Research Centres] on official website. Retrieved 12 August 2010 {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100919163654/http://www.hul.co.in/careers-redesign/carreerschoices/researchanddevelopment/OverviewofResearchCentres/ |date=19 September 2010 }}[[File:Kodai_Lake.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Kodaikanal Lake, one of the most popular tourist attractions in South India, was contaminated following Unilever's illegal dumping of mercury.{{cite news |date=29 September 2016 |title=Prevent mercury pollution |newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |url=http://www.hindu.com/2007/08/23/stories/2007082352980300.htm |url-status=dead |access-date=2019-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071104021328/http://www.hindu.com/2007/08/23/stories/2007082352980300.htm |archive-date=4 November 2007 |orig-year=23 August 2007}}]] == Controversies == === Mercury pollution === {{main|Kodaikanal mercury poisoning}} In 2001 a thermometer factory in [[Kodaikanal]] run by Hindustan Unilever dumped glass contaminated with [[mercury (element)|mercury]] and selling it to scrap merchants.{{cite web |last=Jayaraman |first=Nityanand |date=April 2001 |title=Unilever's Dumping Fever |url=http://www.ban.org/Library/unilevers.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010727143129/http://www.ban.org/Library/unilevers.html |archive-date=27 July 2001 |access-date=31 October 2013 |publisher=Multinational Monitor}} – via Ban.org. Protests by local NGOs and Greenpeace lead to the shutting of the factory in March 2001.{{cite web |date=30 June 2002 |title=Greenpeace wants probe into Kodaikanal mercury pollution |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/Greenpeace-wants-probe-into-Kodaikanal-mercury-pollution/articleshow/14589307.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904121344/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/Greenpeace-wants-probe-into-Kodaikanal-mercury-pollution/articleshow/14589307.cms |archive-date=4 September 2022 |access-date=1 June 2020 |publisher=Times of India}} The issue has since snowballed into a controversy impacting the reputation of the company and led to a series of regulatory and legal confrontations. The issue was eventually resolved in 2016 through an out of court settlement between the company and the affected ex-workers.{{cite web |last=Hiddleston |first=Sarah |date=24 September 2010 |title=Poisoned Ground |url=http://www.hindu.com/fline/fl2719/stories/20100924271900400.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104235613/http://www.hindu.com/fline/fl2719/stories/20100924271900400.htm |archive-date=4 November 2013 |access-date=31 October 2013 |work=Frontline |publisher=The Hindu |volume=27 |issue=19}}{{cite web |last=Jayaraman |first=Nityanand |date=31 July 2010 |title=One gram mercury can kill a 25-acre lake. A plant has leached mercury for 10 years into Kodai |url=http://www.tehelka.com/story_main46.asp?filename=Cr310710onegram.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120925225416/http://www.tehelka.com/story_main46.asp?filename=Cr310710onegram.asp |archive-date=25 September 2012 |access-date=31 October 2013 |work=Tehelka Magazine |publisher=Anant Media Pvt. Ltd. |volume=7 |issue=30}} == Awards == In 2014, Hindustan Unilever Limited received Porter Prize for Creating Shared Value, awarded by the Institute for Competitiveness, India.{{Cite web |date=2014-09-29 |title=Professor Michael E. Porter addressed the gathering at Porter Prize 2014 – Institute for Competitiveness |url=https://www.competitiveness.in/professor-michael-e-porter-addressed-gathering-porter-prize-2014/ |access-date=2025-05-08 |language=en-GB}} It ranked number one on the Forbes list of ‘Most Innovative Companies’ globally for 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/innovative-companies/list/|title=The World's most innovative companies|date=31 October 2014|work=forbes|access-date=29 August 2017|archive-date=4 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121204145428/http://www.forbes.com/innovative-companies/list/|url-status=live}} It also received an award as a 'Conscious Capitalist of the Year' at the 2013 Forbes India Leadership Awards.{{cite web|url=http://forbesindia.com/article/leaderhip-awards-2013/hindustan-unilever-marrying-business-with-social-good/36391/1|title=Conscious Capitalist of the Year|date=31 October 2013|publisher=ForbesIndia|access-date=19 November 2013|archive-date=9 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109065502/http://forbesindia.com/article/leaderhip-awards-2013/hindustan-unilever-marrying-business-with-social-good/36391/1|url-status=live}} Unilever was named the fourth most respected company in India in a survey conducted by Business World in 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.businessworld.in/c/document_library/get_file?uuid=725150d4-f5f6-4bb6-bd27-d1e9aa078ada&groupId=520986|title=Most Respected Company in India|publisher=Businessworld|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514035948/http://www.businessworld.in/c/document_library/get_file?uuid=725150d4-f5f6-4bb6-bd27-d1e9aa078ada&groupId=520986|archive-date=14 May 2014|url-status=dead}} In a 2015 [[Nielsen Holdings|Nielsen]] campus track-business school survey, Hindustan Unilever was among the top employers of choice for B-school students graduating that year. Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) is an Indian's fast-moving consumer goods company, headquartered in Mumbai. It is a subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch company Unilever. Its products include foods, beverages, cleaning agents, personal care products and other consumer staples.
The company was established in India in 1931 as Hindustan Vanaspati Manufacturing Co. Following a merger of constituent groups in 1956, it was renamed Hindustan Lever Limited. The company was renamed again in June 2007 as Hindustan Unilever Limited.
Hindustan Unilever has been at the helm of a lot of controversies, such as dumping highly toxic mercury-contaminated waste in regular dumps, contaminating the land and water of Kodaikanal. (See: Kodaikanal mercury poisoning). The British-Dutch company also faced major flak for an advertising campaign covering the Hindu pilgrimage site at Kumbh Mela in a negative light, calling it a "place where old people get abandoned," a move that was termed racist and insensitive.
In December 2018 HUL announced its acquisition of GlaxoSmithKline India's consumer business for US$3.8 billion in an all-equity merger deal with a 1:4.39 ratio. However, the integration of GSK's 3,800 employees remained uncertain as HUL stated there was no clause for retention of employees in the deal. In April 2020, HUL completed its merger with GlaxoSmithKline Consumer Healthcare (GSKCH India) after completing all legal procedures.
